Perhaps the ocean, with its primeval drama of life and death, will always remind us of where… read article

articles.title: Toxic Productivity: The Real Test Is What You Do in the Gap
articles.highlight: 以工作时长评判“有毒生产力”的清单，会误伤有房贷和正经工作的人；职业心理学有更好的检验方法。
articles.summary: 文章用职业心理学的视角指出：判断“有毒生产力”不能只看工作时长，否则有房贷和正经工作的人也会被误伤。真正的检验在于“空隙”里做什么——能否在任务之间真正停下、恢复，而不是用更多活儿填满每分每秒。实操上可以：把休息排进日程、刻意留出“什么都不做”的间隙、用恢复质量而不是完成数量来评估一天。
articles.failureAnalysis: 关键启示：别用投入时长给自己贴标签，而要在工作间隙主动安排恢复；否则再忙也会因长期耗竭而降低判断力和生产力。
articles.sourceExcerpt: Every list of toxic productivity signs grades you on hours, which flags anyone with a mortgage and a real job. Occupational psychology has a better test

articles.summary: 论文针对想象手写跨被试识别难题，提出频率去相关时间集成（FRED）方法，结合脑电与近红外（EEG-fNIRS）信号进行解码。源文本指出想象手写时间信息丰富但头皮脑电噪声大、个体差异明显，FRED旨在提升跨个体可靠性，相关结果对运动想象脑机接口具有参考意义。
articles.failureAnalysis: 源文本仅给出问题背景和挑战赛信息，未披露FRED的模型细节、实验数据及性能指标，因此无法独立判断其有效性和部署风险。
articles.sourceExcerpt: FRED: Frequency-Decorrelated Temporal Ensembles for EEG–fNIRS Imagined-Handwriting Decoding Xiao Fan, Hongbin Guo, Yubo Han, Yi Zhang Xidian University xdfanxiao@163.com Abstract Imagined handwriting offers a temporally rich paradigm for non- invasive neural decoding, yet reliable recognition across unseen participants remains difficult because scalp EEG is noisy and in- ternally generated stroke sequences vary across individuals. The Multimodal Brain-Computer Interface Grand Challenge provides synchronized EEG and fNIRS for four-class subject-independent handwriting-trajectory classification. We propose FRED, a task- adapted system that models imagined handwriting as a multi- second motor sequence and trains a compact multi-scale tempo- ral network on three complementary EEG frequency views.

en.title: Frequency-Decorrelated Temporal Ensembles for EEG–fNIRS Imagined-Handwriting Decoding
en.highlight: Imagined handwriting offers a temporally rich decoding paradigm, but reliable recognition across unseen participants remains difficult due to noisy EEG and variable stroke sequences.
en.summary: The paper proposes Frequency-Decorrelated Temporal Ensembles (FRED) to decode imagined handwriting from EEG-fNIRS signals, targeting cross-participant reliability. The source text notes that imagined handwriting is temporally rich but scalp EEG is noisy and stroke sequences vary across individuals, and FRED is designed to address this challenge. The work may inform robust motor-imagery brain-computer interfaces.
en.failureAnalysis: The source text provides only background and challenge information, without FRED's architecture, experiments, or quantitative results, so effectiveness and deployment risk cannot be assessed.

articles.title: MageByte-Zero/spec-superflow
articles.selectionReason: AI source passed freshness and evidence-chain gate: GitHub + Community signal
articles.summary: 这是一个 GitHub 上 730 星的 AI 编程工作流插件，宣称在源码层面把 OpenSpec 的规划能力和 Superpowers 的执行纪律结合起来，采用 Spec-first 和契约驱动的方式。它支持 17 个平台和 9 项技能，核心思路是用明确规格约束 AI 编码过程，减少随性输出。对关注 AI 辅助开发工程化、希望让 AI 按规范和契约协作的团队有参考价值。
articles.failureAnalysis: 此类插件容易沦为小众工具：普通开发者已习惯 IDE 自带 AI 或聊天式补全，额外引入一套规划/契约工作流会提高使用门槛。跨 17 平台的深层集成意味着持续的兼容性维护成本，而 Spec-first 的强约束也可能与快速原型阶段需求冲突。开源插件缺乏分发渠道和商业化支撑，若没有形成社区生态，很容易停止维护。

en.highlight: A source-level integration of OpenSpec's planning engine and Superpowers' execution discipline, built as a Spec-first, contract-driven AI coding workflow plugin.
en.summary: This is a GitHub project with 730 stars, an AI coding workflow plugin that claims to combine OpenSpec's planning capability with Superpowers' execution discipline at the source level, using Spec-first and contract-driven methods. It supports 17 platforms and 9 skills, with the core idea of using explicit specs to constrain AI coding and reduce arbitrary output. It is a useful reference for teams interested in engineering AI-assisted development and making AI collaborate under clear contracts.
en.failureAnalysis: The plugin risks staying a niche tool because most developers already use IDE-native AI or chat-style completion, and adding a planning/contract workflow raises the adoption barrier. Maintaining deep integrations across 17 platforms is costly, and the Spec-first constraint may clash with fast prototyping; without strong community or distribution, an open-source plugin can easily become unmaintained.
